jordan_acme: Heads up — our prod tenant acct_0a1b2c3d ran out of monthly credits mid-import at 09:12 UTC. Dashboard still showed ~12k tokens but API returns 429 with body '{"error":"quota.exhausted","code":429}'. Help? :weary:

sarah_support: Sorry for the interruption. Can you paste the root request id or a sample failing request? Also were these streaming calls or the bulk embed job you mentioned?

jordan_acme: This was the bulk embed pipeline (not streaming) — about 120 concurrent workers hitting the embeddings endpoint with retries. Sample curl from a worker below.

jordan_acme: ```
curl -i https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-acme-xxxxx" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-embed-1","input":["doc1","doc2"]}'
```

jordan_acme: Worker log response:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
X-RateLimit-Limit: 120000
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1712345800

{"error":"quota.exhausted","code":429,"message":"monthly token bucket empty"}
```

devon_infra: tagging infra. We see a sharp spike at 09:11:40 with many short retries. Two things are likely: 1) frontend/UI showed stale cache of the tenant balance for ~20-40s while the refill/accounting propagated, 2) retries without an idempotency key caused duplicate consumptions.

sarah_support: Agreed. If the worker retried after the server already accepted the request, and no Idempotency-Key was provided, the retry will be charged as a separate invocation. Please share one raw request (you did, thanks) and whether your client lib sends any idempotency header.

jordan_acme: Our retry library uses backoff+jit but does not add Idempotency-Key. Does Redwood support dedupe via a header?

devon_infra: Yes — we dedupe when requests include a stable Idempotency-Key per logical operation. Without it, each retry is treated as a distinct call. We can correlate on identical payloads but it's heuristic and not reliable under high concurrency.

quota-bot: auto-case created: CASE-8022. Assigned to infra/usage for detailed accounting. ETA initial triage 3h.

sarah_support: Short-term mitigation: lower concurrency (<=32), add exponential backoff with jitter, and implement Idempotency-Key. We can also offer a one-time emergency top-up to get you unblocked while we audit counts. Long-term: batch size <=8, client-side dedupe, and idempotency per document/process.

jordan_acme: Can you confirm whether retries are actually double-counting in our case? We saw many 502/timeout responses and then retries.

devon_infra: We traced matching payload hashes and request signatures during the spike — there are many matching pairs that indicate the client retried after the server accepted. So yes, duplicates were charged. Also, the edge quota cache returned pre-spike balance for ~30s which made the UI show tokens that were already consumed.

sarah_support: For implementation, include header:
```
Idempotency-Key: <uuid-v4>
```
Use one UUID per logical unit (e.g., per uploaded document or per batch), keep it stable across retries. Handle 429s with Retry-After and exponential backoff.

devon_infra: We scheduled a +15000 token emergency top-up for acct_0a1b2c3d; it should be visible in the UI within 90s. We'll put a detailed RCA and logs into CASE-8022 once done. We can also discuss a short-lived server-side override to ignore obvious duplicate retries during your patch, but that requires authorization.

jordan_acme: Top-up received — thanks. We'll roll idempotency keys and reduce concurrency today. Can you share a short client snippet for generating the Idempotency-Key?

sarah_support: Example (Node):
```
const idempotencyKey = require('crypto').randomUUID();
fetch(url, { headers: { 'Authorization': `Bearer ${KEY}`, 'Idempotency-Key': idempotencyKey } });
```
Use the same key for retries of the same logical request.

jordan_acme: Perfect. Appreciate the quick help. We'll follow up in CASE-8022 if anything else pops up. :pray:
